note: Register of tabnas runtime dependencies that differ between this repository's ports (tabnas/admin ADR-24). tools/port-deps.cjs fails on a difference that is not listed here, and on an entry that no longer matches the manifests, so the list cannot outlive what it records. Every entry states the ports that have the dependency today, the reason, and the repair.

parser.reason: TypeScript: ts/package.json lists '@tabnas/parser' under peerDependencies, with peerDependenciesMeta marking it optional, and the only import of it in ts/src is type-only, `import type { Tabnas, Rule } from '@tabnas/parser'` in ts/src/adder.ts, the adder test grammar published as the subpath export `./adder`; `import type` is erased on compile, so only adder's type declarations name the engine, and ts/test/adder.test.js takes the engine as a value through the devDependency. Go: the same grammar is go/adder/adder.go, which imports github.com/tabnas/parser/go but belongs to a separate module (go/adder/go.mod, github.com/tabnas/support/go/adder, which AGENTS.md calls private and never tagged); go/go.mod has no require at all, and no .go file of the module at go/ imports the engine. Rust: the grammar is the separate, unpublished crate `tabnas-support-adder` (rs/adder/Cargo.toml depends on `tabnas-parser`, and rs/Cargo.toml excludes `adder/**`), while rs/Cargo.toml's one dependency is the optional `serde_json` and nothing in rs/src uses the `tabnas` crate.
parser.repair: Either the TypeScript port splits the adder out as Go and Rust do: ts/src/adder.ts and the `./adder` export move to a package of their own that peers on '@tabnas/parser' (published, or private as the Go module and the Rust crate are), and ts/package.json drops the peer and its peerDependenciesMeta entry, leaving the support package with no tabnas dependency in any port. Or Go and Rust take the adder back in: rs/Cargo.toml could gate it behind an optional feature, but Go modules have no optional requirement, so go/go.mod would require the engine outright, against AGENTS.md ("The Go support module and the Rust support crate take no dependencies"). Ruled intentional by the maintainer on 2026-10-06: the optional, type-only peer serves the `./adder` export, while Go and Rust keep the adder in a separate private module and crate; the difference stays and no repair is owed.
